findings.description: SHEET-MARK-001's phrase "a bounded timeout" reads as temporal, and all three A-outputs unanimously built literal wall-clock mechanisms for it: std::time::Duration + Instant-based deadlines with a configurable poll_interval/timeout (A1 defaults 500ms/30s; A3 defaults 500ms/30s via Default for SettleConfig; A2 leaves interval caller-supplied but still Instant-deadline-based) and thread::sleep between polls. The real code's bound is nothing like this: sheets_view::SettleConfig { max_polls: u32 } (default 8) is a pure poll-COUNT ceiling -- read_marks's loop calls client.read_price_pass() up to max_polls times with NO Duration, Instant, or sleep anywhere in the crate (the doc comment even concedes pacing is deferred to "runtime's real client", but no such pacing exists in any shipped adapter -- ViewSheetsAdapter::read_price_pass is one bare read per call). So the settle pass has no temporal bound at all: 8 fast reads resolve in milliseconds, 8 slow/hung reads could stall indefinitely -- only iteration count is constrained. All three B-outputs, working purely from code, converge exactly on this (max_polls, default 8, poll-count not duration) and never reconstruct a time-based interpretation -- confirming spec-vs-code drift on both sides of the same seam: the spec's word "timeout" forces a time-based A-side invention while the code's real mechanism is count-based with zero built-in pacing.

The code's cell classification is a 3-way taxonomy with a specific, non-obvious carve-out that SHEET-MARK-001's binary "numeric or terminally errored" framing doesn't state and that none of the A-outputs invent. price_reading_from_cells (adapters.rs): trimmed-empty, case-insensitive "Loading...", or EXACTLY "#N/A" -> PriceReading::Transient (kept polling, eligible for prior-mark carry-forward -- i.e. NOT treated as "terminally errored" even though it's literally an error string); any OTHER #-prefixed text (#ERROR!, #REF!, etc.) -> Permanent (terminal); anything else non-numeric -> also Permanent. A persistent #N/A can therefore NEVER be classified as the spec's "terminally errored" outcome -- it only ever exits the loop via poll-bound exhaustion (then carry-forward-or-TimedOut), never via being recognized as an error. All three B-outputs state this exact asymmetric rule with the same string literals ("#N/A" exact vs. any other #-prefix); all three A-outputs instead treat ANY #-prefixed text as immediately terminal -- a simpler, textually-reasonable reading of "terminally errored" that the real code contradicts.

A whole prior-mark carry-forward state machine is invisible in SHEET-MARK-001's text and absent from all three A-outputs (reasonably -- nothing in the given EARS text mentions a prior marks map at all). Real read_marks(client, symbols, prior: &BTreeMap<Symbol, Mark>, cfg): when the poll bound (max_polls) is reached and a symbol is still Transient/absent, IF a prior mark exists it is carried forward UNCHANGED and NOT recorded degraded; only when no prior mark exists does it degrade DegradeReason::TimedOut. Pinned by sheets-view/tests/marks.rs::transient_keeps_prior_mark_and_retries_degrades_only_after_window and ::no_prior_mark_stays_transient_degrades_after_window. All three B-outputs reconstruct this precisely (as a distinct State-driven/Unwanted-behavior clause); this is a materially significant behavior (a stale price can silently persist rather than nulling the position) with zero textual basis in the given spec.

The price->Cents conversion co-located with this settle pass (price_to_cents) enforces a specific rounding rule and degrade taxonomy SHEET-MARK-001 never mentions: round_half_to_even(price_usd x 100) via integer x1,000,000 micro-scaling, with DegradeReason::SubCent for any result <=0 cents (covering exact 0.0, negative, and positive-rounds-to-zero) and DegradeReason::Permanent for non-finite (NaN/+-Infinity) input. All three B-outputs reconstruct this identically, including the banker's-rounding examples (1.005->1.00, 1.015->1.02) pinned by usd_price_converts_to_cents_round_half_to_even. This likely belongs to a sibling SHEET-MARK-* requirement not shown here, so it's scoped-adjacent rather than a pure omission -- but relative to the ONE EARS text given, it is pure code-side surplus, and none of the A-outputs derive Cents-conversion or sub-cent degrade logic from SHEET-MARK-001's text (reasonably, since it isn't there).

Minor boundary/scope surpluses, unanimous across B1/B2/B3, none anticipated by any A-output: (a) a not-yet-created Positions tab makes read_price_pass return an empty PricePass rather than an error (is_missing_tab short-circuit in ViewSheetsAdapter::read_price_pass); (b) a companion Quote Date column (index 12) is parsed as i32 days-since-epoch and stamped onto every settled mark, defaulting to Date(0) if absent/unparseable -- SHEET-MARK-001 discusses only the Price cell, never a quote-date field; (c) a transport-level Err from read_price_pass propagates immediately and yields literally no MarksProduced (never an empty map, which would misread as "everything degraded") -- asserted by transport_failure_propagates_error_does_not_emit_empty_marks. Notably the three A-outputs actively disagree with each other on point (c): A1 propagates a wrapped error (closest to real behavior), A2's settle_marks has no error path at all, and A3 treats a mid-poll transport Err as transient/retry-worthy -- the opposite of the real code's immediate-propagate behavior. This is invented territory the given spec text doesn't govern, so it's noted mainly as evidence of A-fleet disagreement on ungoverned ground rather than a clean spec-vs-code finding.

notes: SHEET-MARK-001 as given is a single terse EARS line; the code region it anchors (sheets_view::read_marks/price_to_cents + the ViewSheetsAdapter classification helper) is considerably richer. The single most load-bearing finding is the timeout-vs-poll-count mismatch (#1), since it's the one place both fleets independently converge on the SAME underlying tension: the spec's temporal word choice versus the code's purely iteration-count-bounded, unpaced loop. The remaining findings (#2-#5) are strong, highly-stable B-side-only surpluses -- some (prior-carry-forward, #N/A-as-perpetually-transient) are squarely inside SHEET-MARK-001's subject matter and materially change runtime behavior; others (price_to_cents rounding/degrade, quote-date parsing) plausibly belong to sibling SHEET-MARK-* requirements not shown, so I've flagged that caveat rather than treating them as clean omissions. Both A and B fleets were highly internally consistent, so this is a confident BD-DRIFT read rather than a borderline/blind call.
